beats.say: When a scammer gets into a partner's mailbox, they reply in your old thread. Subject and signature look familiar.
A password protected archive is a warning sign. The password hides the file from antivirus checks.

body.text: the final contract is in the archive.
If you do not sign today, the price changes.

beats.say: Even in a familiar thread, do not rush to open an unexpected attachment or urgent request.
If in doubt, call the partner on a number you know and ask if they sent the file.

scenes.prompt: Find what changed in this reply.

body.text: the final contract and payment schedule are attached.
Sign in with your work email to open it.
> Hi. I will send the revised draft on Monday, no rush. Elchin

spots.label: Changed tone
spots.explain: He used to write "Hi", now "Dear partner". A sudden change of tone suggests someone else is writing.

spots.label: HTML attachment
spots.explain: Contracts come as PDF or Word. An HTML attachment usually opens a fake sign-in page.

spots.label: Sign-in request
spots.explain: Opening an attachment never needs your password. A file that asks for it wants to steal it.

spots.label: Sudden rush
spots.explain: The earlier mail said "no rush". A sudden deadline is a scammer's tool.

scenes.title: Project thread
scenes.intro: You have a long thread with Kur Tikinti. Check the new replies: which are real and which come from a hijacked mailbox?

body.text: Hi. We took your comments into account, the revised draft is attached.
Call me if you have questions. Elchin

actions.label: Open attachment
actions.feedback: An expected PDF, the usual tone, no pressure. This is normal work mail.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: There is no warning sign here. The file is expected and fits the thread.

body.text: the final contract is in the archive.
If you do not sign today, the price changes.

steps.say: Look at the archive and the password.

actions.label: Open attachment
actions.feedback: Malware can hide in a password protected archive, because antivirus cannot look inside.

actions.label: Call Elchin on a known number
actions.feedback: Great. If Elchin did not send it, his mailbox is hijacked and he needs to know.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right: sudden rush, protected archive and a new tone. Reporting protects the team too.

actions.label: Reply: is this you?
actions.feedback: The reply goes to the hijacked mailbox and the scammer says yes. Call instead.

body.text: The schedule is in a protected file. Open it and sign in with your work email.

actions.label: Open attachment
actions.feedback: The HTML file opens a fake sign-in page in the browser. You typed nothing yet, close it.

actions.label: Sign in
actions.feedback: The scammer now has your password. Change it now and tell security.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right. A payment schedule needs no password, and an HTML attachment is a typical trap.

body.text: This time pay the advance to our partner company's account, details attached.

actions.label: Call a known number to check
actions.feedback: Right. A request to pay another company is confirmed only by phone.

actions.label: Reply: we accept the details
actions.feedback: The advance would go to the scammer. A familiar thread does not prove a new account.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Good step. Two suspicious mails in one thread is a serious signal.

body.text: Hi, we suggest a change to clause 5. Let us discuss it at tomorrow's meeting.

actions.label: Reply
actions.feedback: An internal address, no attachment or link, nothing asked. This is normal mail.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: This mail shows no signs. Save reports for suspicious mail.

cards.explain: An expected document, a normal format and a known sender. Fine to open.
A password protected archive hides from antivirus. Call the sender and ask.
A contract is never an HTML file. Such a file opens a fake sign-in page.
From an internal department, agreed in advance. No warning sign.
The real type is .exe, a program. An invoice is never a program.

nodes.text: You opened the protected archive. There was no contract inside, just a strange file, and the screen went dark for a moment.

choices.label: Disconnect from the network and call security
choices.feedback: Right. Disconnecting stops the spread, and the call brings in the team.

choices.label: Shut the computer down at once
choices.feedback: Shutting down can erase evidence in memory. Unless your procedure says otherwise, leave it on and disconnect it.

choices.label: Tell no one, probably nothing happened
choices.feedback: Malware works quietly and can spread across the network. Reporting a mistake fast is not shameful, it saves the day.

nodes.text: Thank you. Is the email still in your mailbox? And did you tell Kur Tikinti?
nodes.speaker: Security team
nodes.spoken: Thank you. <breath> Is the email still in your mailbox? And did you tell Kur Tikinti?

choices.label: I kept the email, and I call Elchin on a known number
choices.feedback: Great. The email is evidence, and the partner must learn their mailbox was hijacked.

choices.label: I deleted the email to leave no trace
choices.feedback: The email is needed for the investigation. Next time keep it and follow security's instructions.

choices.label: I reply to Elchin in the same thread
choices.feedback: The scammer reads that mailbox. Tell the partner by phone.

points: A familiar thread can be hijacked too
Before opening a protected archive or HTML file, call and check
If you opened it, disconnect and report at once
